title: Modal Verbs
explanation: Modal verbs — **können** (can), **müssen** (must), **wollen** (want to), **dürfen** (may), **sollen** (should), **mögen** (like to) — express ability, necessity, desire, or permission. They're irregular in the singular, and they push the main verb to the very end of the sentence as a plain infinitive.

exercises.prompt: Where does the main verb go in a sentence with a modal verb?
options: At the end of the sentence, as an infinitive
At the start of the sentence
exercises.answer: At the end of the sentence, as an infinitive
